content.value_statement: Agents often need simple dice rolls for games, examples, or randomized test values. This skill runs a Rust dice roller through Enact and returns individual rolls with the total.
actual_capabilities: Rolls between 1 and 100 dice in a single request.
Supports dice with 2 to 100 sides, including common tabletop dice such as d6, d20, and d100.
Returns individual roll values plus the total, side count, and dice count.
Provides CLI examples for Enact users and MCP invocation guidance for agents.
Builds and runs a small Rust executable inside the Enact tool flow.
limitations: Uses a simple time-seeded generator and is not suitable for cryptographic randomness or fairness-critical wagering.
Clamps inputs to 2-100 sides and 1-100 dice rather than supporting arbitrary dice expressions.
Returns numeric roll results only; it does not apply tabletop rules, modifiers, advantage, or success thresholds by itself.
Requires an Enact-compatible runtime or MCP setup before agents can call it.

use_cases.title: Run Tabletop Rolls
use_cases.description: Roll common dice combinations during lightweight role-playing sessions and summarize the individual results and total.

use_cases.title: Create Random Test Values
use_cases.description: Generate bounded random integers for demos, examples, or simple testing workflows where reproducible security-grade randomness is not required.

use_cases.title: Study Enact Tool Patterns
use_cases.description: Use a compact Rust implementation to understand Enact input schemas, output schemas, CLI invocation, and MCP-facing documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Roll a Standard Die
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dice roll skill to roll one six-sided die and tell me the result.

prompt_templates.title: Roll Tabletop Damage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the dice roll skill to roll three eight-sided dice, then report each die and the total damage.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Stat Rolls
prompt_templates.prompt: Call the dice roll skill six times with four six-sided dice each, then list the six totals in descending order.

prompt_templates.title: Check Bounded Random Samples
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the dice roll skill with 20 sides and 10 dice, verify every value is within range, and summarize the individual rolls and total.

output_examples.output: Rolled 2d6: the individual rolls were 3 and 5, for a total of 8.

output_examples.input: Roll one twenty-sided die for an attack check.
output_examples.output: Rolled 1d20: the result was 17, with a total of 17.

output_examples.input: Roll four six-sided dice for a stat result.
output_examples.output: Rolled 4d6: the individual rolls were 6, 4, 3, and 2, for a total of 15.

best_practices: Specify both the number of sides and the dice count so the agent does not rely on defaults accidentally.
Use the tool for games, demos, and simple bounded randomness rather than security-sensitive decisions.
Ask the agent to report both individual rolls and totals when the distinction matters.
anti_patterns: Do not use the output as cryptographic randomness, gambling fairness proof, or security token material.
Do not expect the skill to parse compound dice notation, modifiers, or game rules unless the agent handles that logic separately.
Do not request values outside the documented input limits and expect the exact out-of-range request to be preserved.

faq.question: Can this skill roll a d20?
faq.answer: Yes. Request one die with 20 sides to produce a standard d20 roll.

faq.question: How many dice can it roll at once?
faq.answer: It supports 1 to 100 dice per request.

faq.question: What side counts are supported?
faq.answer: It supports dice with 2 to 100 sides, including d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20, and d100.

faq.question: Is the randomness cryptographically secure?
faq.answer: No. The implementation uses a simple time-seeded generator, so it is appropriate for casual rolls and examples only.

faq.question: What does the skill return?
faq.answer: It returns the individual die results, the total, the side count, and the number of dice rolled.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes, when the skill is installed through an Enact-compatible setup that exposes it to Claude, Codex, or Claude Code via the supported tool interface.
